en: Having fixed upon his bow an arrow intoxicated by drinking the blood from the chest-thoraxes of the host of enemies, he stands as the destroyer of the heat within my heart-lotus.
May the son of Paśupati, who wears a peacock feather as an ornament, who is the refuge of all, and who is ever vigilant, protect us always. || 1 ||

O Ocean of Compassion, may You—who were born in ancient times as the son of Śambhu, the forest-dweller devoted to Girijā, for the sake of hunting; who became renowned as one appearing in the form of a Kirāta to protect the world;
who bear a bow and a dagger, possess a deep luster, and shine with a peacock-feather ornament—protect me, who am terrified by hosts of enemies, at all times.
O embodied one, having pierced the chest of that enemy who constantly and violently oppresses me— who have you as my sole refuge— with a small knife.
O Lord, O illustrious one who has assumed the form of a Kirāta, by the lotus-like hand that shines forth from you, the sharp edge [of the arrow] was rendered ineffective against the evil-minded one.
Therefore, O Blessed One, swiftly bestow their lives upon Antaka, the son of Kālārī.
Pierced in my vital organs by the wicked words of the arrogant and unpeaceful-minded enemies, which were like burning arrows, I am tormented.
While I am thus exceedingly weary,
you appear before my mind, bearing a dagger and a bow.
O Lord, O God in the form of a Kirāta, destroy the host of adversaries in an instant! || 4 ||

O bestower of all aims, apart from you who assume the form of a Kirāta to punish enemies, quickly strike at the vital organs with arrows released from your bow those wicked thieves who delight in robbing me of my wealth and dharma.
O son of the Enemy of Tripura, I see no other refuge here; I have taken refuge in you alone. || 5 ||

O Lord, O Son of Gaurī, O Sovereign of Deities, O You who have assumed the form of a Kirāta, protect me! Having destroyed all those evil planets—hosts of Yakṣas, Pretas, Piśācas, and Bhūtas, who are terrifying, bringers of misery, and whose minds long for human blood, being incited by enemies—with the twanging sounds of your bowstring. May you protect me.

O God of gods, Lord of the three worlds, assume the form of a Śabara and destroy my wicked enemies—those intent on harming me, who are experts in the skillful commencement of rites such as subjugation, paralyzing, and killing; those who, disguised by Māyā, give poison with food and drink, and who are skilled in the performance of evil deeds. O Lord, [protect] me, whose sole devotion is fixed upon Your lotus feet!

O Son of Girīśa, may you forgive all those men who, even though I am innocent and constantly bowing at your feet, persistently seek to find faults with me through their body, mind, or speech; and may you likewise endure the floods of my threefold afflictions, for I have taken refuge in you alone, O Lord, as my protector from fear in the form of a Śabara.

Dragged away by the king’s soldiers, constantly humiliated by wicked enemies and others even more cruel, I am submerged in the ocean of calamity, afflicted by suffering. Alas, alas! O Lord, what shall I do? I bow to You, who wear the guise of a hunter and grant desired objects; You are the supreme deity. O Protector, O Friend of the helpless, have mercy upon me! 9.
He who constantly recites this *Kirātāṣṭaka* hymn with tranquil senses quickly brings even kings of long-standing enmity under his control.
Having subdued wicked people who oppose him and even malevolent planets, he ultimately attains the eternal, divine state, free from the fear of Yama’s messengers. (10)
Thus ends the Kirātāṣṭaka.
